facts.fact: The Saluda River begins in the Blue Ridge Mountains and continues through the Piedmont before joining the Congaree River near Columbia.

facts.fact: The Saluda River is divided into Upper, Middle, and Lower Saluda sections.
facts.quote: The waterway is divided into distinct sections - Upper, Middle, and Lower Saluda - each providing unique fishing experiences.

facts.fact: The Lower Saluda features cold, clear water released from Lake Murray Dam, creating a tailwater fishery supporting trout through hot summers.
facts.quote: The Lower Saluda, in particular, is renowned for its cold, clear water released from the bottom of Lake Murray Dam, creating a tailwater fishery that supports trout even during South Carolina's hot summers.
facts.source: Saluda River Fishing in South Carolina

facts.fact: In South Carolina, navigable waterways that can be floated and used as a public highway are open to recreational use up to the high water mark.

facts.fact: Children under 16 in South Carolina do not need a fishing license unless engaged in commercial activity or using non-game fish devices.
facts.quote: Children under the age of 16 are not required to purchase a hunting or fishing license unless they are engaged in commercial activity or using any non-game fish devices (traps, trotlines, gill nets, hoop nets, set hooks, jugs.)
facts.source: Saluda River Fishing in South Carolina

facts.fact: The North Saluda River is located in the South Carolina mountains.
facts.quote: Tucked away in the South Carolina mountains, the North Saluda River is a heavily stocked trout fishery known for steady, reliable action.
facts.source: North Saluda River Trout Fishing, South Carolina (Stocked Weekly) | What Works Now

facts.fact: The North Saluda River is a heavily stocked trout fishery with weekly trout plants in the spring.
facts.quote: the North Saluda River is a heavily stocked trout fishery known for steady, reliable action. With weekly trout plants keeping the river full of trout in the spring, it’s a go-to destination for anglers.
facts.source: North Saluda River Trout Fishing, South Carolina (Stocked Weekly) | What Works Now

facts.fact: The Saluda River supports diverse fish species including trout, bass, and catfish.
facts.quote: The Saluda River is a prime fishing destination in South Carolina, known for its diverse fish species and scenic beauty. Anglers flock to this river year-round to target trout, bass, catfish, and other popular species.
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: The Lower Saluda River is a tailwater section below Lake Murray Dam known for year-round cold-water trout habitats supporting rainbow and brown trout.
facts.quote: One of the most notable features is the Lower Saluda River, a tailwater section below Lake Murray Dam. This section benefits from cold water releases, creating a unique environment where trout thrive year-round — a rarity in the warm climate of South Carolina. This cold-water habitat offers consistent trout fishing opportunities, particularly for rainbow and brown trout.
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: The Upper Saluda River is known for smallmouth bass, largemouth bass, and catfish.
facts.quote: The upper Saluda River is known for smallmouth bass, largemouth bass, and catfish, while the middle and lower sections offer excellent trout fishing opportunities.
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: The Lower Saluda River is heavily stocked with rainbow and brown trout during cooler months.
facts.quote: This section is heavily stocked during cooler months, providing a reliable fishery even in the heart of South Carolina’s warmer climate.
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: Striped bass are common in the Lower Saluda River, especially during spring and fall runs.
facts.quote: Striped bass are also common in this area, especially during spring and fall runs.
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: Public access points along the Saluda River include Saluda Shoals Park and Riverbanks Zoo.
facts.quote: Locations like Saluda Shoals Park and Riverbanks Zoo provide convenient entry points for waders, kayakers, and boat anglers alike.
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: Additional public access points for the Saluda River include Hope Ferry Landing and the Irmo Side of Lake Murray Dam.
facts.quote:
Hope Ferry Landing: This boat ramp is ideal for anglers with larger boats seeking deeper water for striped bass and catfish. The ramp provides easy access to some of the most productive pools and eddies along the Lower Saluda River.

Irmo Side of Lake Murray Dam: This access point provides direct entry to the coldest tailwater section, ideal for targeting trophy trout and striped bass during seaso
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: The Middle Saluda River is a designated trout fishery stocked regularly with rainbow and brown trout.
facts.quote: Flowing through Jones Gap State Park and the surrounding foothills, this section is a designated trout fishery, stocked regularly with rainbow and brown trout.
facts.source: Top Saluda River Fishing Spots in South Carolina

facts.fact: The coldwater fishery in the Lower Saluda River is maintained by annual trout stockings by DNR of approximately 30,000 trout, with about 75% brown trout and 25% rainbow trout.
facts.quote: The coldwater fishery is possible because of the cooler than normal water released from Lake Murray, and is maintained by annual trout stockings by DNR of approximately 30,000 trout, with about 75% brown trout and 25% rainbow trout.
facts.source: Lower Saluda River

facts.fact: Typical length at stocking for trout in the Lower Saluda River is from 7 to 10 inches.
facts.quote: Typical length at stocking is from 7 to 10 inches, but rainbow trout of 4 to 8 pounds have been caught, indicating some carryover of fish from year to year in spite of low levels of dissolved oxygen in the fall months.
facts.source: Lower Saluda River

facts.fact: Warmwater species occurring in the lower Saluda River include chain pickerel, redbreast sunfish, redear sunfish, bluegill, largemouth bass, carp, channel catfish, spotted sucker, yellow perch, sandbar shiner, and gizzard shad.
facts.quote: Warmwater species occurring in the lower Saluda River include chain pickerel, redbreast sunfish, redear sunfish, bluegill, largemouth bass, carp, channel catfish, spotted sucker, yellow perch, sandbar shiner, and gizzard shad.
facts.source: Lower Saluda River

facts.fact: DHEC has issued a public health advisory limiting consumption of largemouth bass, chain pickerel, and bowfin (mudfish) to one meal per week in the Saluda River from the Dam to its confluence with the Broad River due to high levels of mercury.
facts.quote: Fish flesh analysis from the Saluda River below Lake Murray Dam indicates high levels of mercury (Hg). Consequently, DHEC has issued a public health advisory for consuming certain fish species in the Saluda River from the Dam to its confluence with the Broad River. They advise that people limit consumption of largemouth bass, chain pickerel, and bowfin (mudfish) to one meal per week.
facts.source: Lower Saluda River

facts.fact: Daily average dissolved oxygen in the Lower Saluda River has increased from 2.7 mg/L to 7.2 mg/L.
facts.quote: Even though the daily average DO has increased from 2.7 mg/L to 7.2 mg/L and instantaneous levels have improved, DO levels still do not meet state water quality standards all the time.
facts.source: Lower Saluda River
